extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and writers interested in mythology, narrative structure, and the hero's journey
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the monomyth (the hero's journey) as a narrative structure for myths and stories, summarizing stages, archetypal roles, and analytic influences useful for writers, scholars, and artists.

rubrics_metrics.name: The monomyth / "the hero's adventure" (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A hero ventures forth from the world of common day into a region of supernatural wonder: fabulous forces are there encountered and a decisive victory is won: the hero comes back from this mysterious adventure with the power to bestow boons on his fellow man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one-sentence summary encapsulates the monomyth's overall arc (departure → initiation → return) and is the organizing principle for the stages that follow. It is presented as a general pattern observed across many world myths and as a usable template for storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary World
rubrics_metrics.description: The starting condition: 'the world of common day' from which the hero ventures forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the hero's baseline life and context; provides contrast to the supernatural world and grounds the character so the audience can perceive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to Adventure
rubrics_metrics.description: An event or prompt that requires the hero to depart from the ordinary world and begin the journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as the inciting incident that disrupts the hero's status quo and motivates departure; should be clearly linked to stakes or an opportunity for change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: A helper figure who assists the hero preparing for and crossing into the adventure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors provide knowledge, tools, or training that enable the hero to face the unknown; may be literal or symbolic and often catalyze the crossing of the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarded Threshold / Crossing the Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of leaving the ordinary world and entering a supernatural or unfamiliar realm where familiar laws do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often dramatized as a barrier or test; crossing signals commitment to the journey and transformation of the hero's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural World (special world)
rubrics_metrics.description: The realm encountered after crossing the threshold, characterized by different rules, dangers, and possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This zone enables trials and transformations that cannot occur within the ordinary world; it amplifies symbolic and literal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Road of Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of tests, tasks, or ordeals that the hero must undergo in the special world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trials shape and prove the hero, often escalating in difficulty and revealing strengths, flaws, and growth opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allies
rubrics_metrics.description: Companions or helpers who assist the hero during the journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allies can offer practical help, emotional support, or contrasting perspectives; they can also highlight the hero's leadership and relational growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordeal (the greatest challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The central, often climactic test of the journey — described as the greatest challenge the hero faces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ordeal frequently involves confronting death, deepest fear, or a major antagonistic force; success marks a turning point and usually precedes reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward / Boon
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize, knowledge, or power the hero receives after overcoming the ordeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The boon may be literal (treasure, power) or symbolic (insight, reconciliation) and is what the hero ultimately brings back to benefit others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death and Resurrection (metaphorical)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metaphorical (or literal) death and subsequent rebirth that marks transformative change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motif signals deep psychological or social transformation; it often occurs at the ordeal and is central to the hero's internal renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return / Road Back / Application of the Boon
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero's decision and process of coming back to the ordinary world and using the boon to improve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return may entail further trials; successful reintegration demonstrates the value of the journey and completes the narrative cycle by showing benefit to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure / Initiation / Return (three-part schema)
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-level structuring into three phases: Departure (Separation), Initiation, and Return, derived from rites of passage scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell maps many specific steps into these three broad movements; writers can use this triad as a macro-structure for plotting and thematic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Jungian archetypes and unconscious forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative employs Jungian archetypal figures and the concept of the collective unconscious as explanatory tools for recurring mythic motifs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campbell's analysis foregrounds archetypal roles (mentor, shadow, trickster, etc.) and unconscious dynamics; authors and analysts may intentionally incorporate or reference archetypes to evoke universal resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of Freudian concepts and rites-of-passage theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Campbell's model integrates Freudian ideas (e.g., Oedipal themes) and Arnold van Gennep's rites-of-passage (separation, transition, incorporation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theoretical grounding suggests evaluating stories for underlying psychosocial and ritual structures; such elements can deepen thematic complexity if used deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility/variance of the monomyth stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Many myths vary in inclusion and sequence of the monomyth stages; the monomyth is a general pattern rather than a rigid checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should treat the stages as adaptable: not every story needs every step or the same order, and meaningful variants can strengthen originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability to modern storytelling (influence and adaptation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The monomyth can be consciously applied by modern writers and artists as a guide for structuring narratives (e.g., film, games, novels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites concrete examples (George Lucas/Star Wars, Journey the game, Christopher Vogler's memo and The Writer's Journey) illustrating how the schema has been used as a practical blueprint for scripts and games; practitioners may adapt the pattern to medium-specific needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artists as 'magical helpers' — using myth to evoke psychological transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists can function like 'magical helpers' who evoke symbols and motifs connecting audiences to deeper selves and helping them along heroic journeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescriptive idea suggests a criterion for creative work: use symbolic arrangement and motif to facilitate audience psychological engagement and transformation.
